questions.question: In R, when is the condition of a `while (condition) { ... }` loop evaluated?
options: Before every pass, so the body runs zero times if it is `FALSE` at the start.
After every pass, so the body always runs at least once before any check.
Only once, before the first pass; then the body repeats until R is stopped.
Before every pass, but the first pass runs whatever the condition says.

questions.question: In `while (balance > 0) { balance <- balance - payment; months <- months + 1 }`, the first line of a pass makes `balance` negative. What happens to the second line of that pass?
options: It is skipped: the loop ends at the line where the condition turns `FALSE`.
It is skipped for this pass, and the loop goes on with the next pass.
It still runs: the condition is checked again only before the next pass.
It still runs, and R then runs one more full pass before checking again.

questions.question: A `while` loop in RStudio keeps running because its counter is never updated. What should you do?
options: Interrupt R with Esc or the Stop button, then add the missing update.
Close the script file in the editor, which stops the code it started.
Wait, since R ends every loop with an error after a fixed number of passes.
Run the corrected loop, which replaces the one that is still running.

questions.question: Which of these tasks is a natural fit for a `while` loop rather than a `for` loop?
options: Adding up the elements of a vector `x` whose length is known.
Printing the squares of the whole numbers from 1 to 10.
Filling a vector `z` with one value for each element of `x`.
Repaying a loan year by year until the balance is not positive.

questions.question: What does R print for `k` after `x <- 50; k <- 0; while (x > 1) { x <- x / 2; k <- k + 1 }; k`?
The loop `i <- 1; s <- 0; while (i <= 5 & s < 5) { s <- s + i; i <- i + 1 }` has two stopping conditions joined by `&`. What is `s` when it ends?
The loop `s <- 0; i <- 10; while (i > 0) { s <- s + i }` never ends. Which change makes it stop with `s` equal to 55?
options: Add `i <- i - 1` after `s <- s + i`, inside the braces.
Add `i <- i + 1` after `s <- s + i`, inside the braces.
Add `i <- i - 1` on a new line after the closing brace.
Change the condition to `i >= 0`, keeping the body as it is.

questions.question: What does R print for `n` after `n <- 1; while (n < 100) n <- n * 2; n`?
The loop `while (...) x <- x + 1` should keep adding 1 until every element of `x <- c(12, 5)` is at least 10. Which condition does that in R 4.3?
What is `i` after `x <- c(4, 8, 1); i <- 1; s <- 0; while (i <= length(x)) { s <- s + x[i]; i <- i + 1 }`?
An iteration uses `while (change > tol & iter < iterMax)`, increasing `iter` by 1 per pass. After the loop, `iter` equals `iterMax`. What can you conclude?
options: It may have stopped at the cap; `change <= tol` tells whether it converged.
The method did not converge, since the loop ran out of passes.
The method converged, since the loop only ends once `change <= tol`.
The loop ended with an error, since `iter` must stay below `iterMax`.

questions.question: A `while` loop improves a guess until two successive guesses differ by less than $10^{-7}$. Which statement about the final guess is correct?
options: Its distance to the true value is guaranteed to be below $10^{-7}$.
A small change is a stopping rule; it does not prove the error is small.
Its distance to the true value equals the last change between guesses.
It must equal the true value, as the guesses have stopped changing.

questions.question: Which `while` loop prints the same numbers as `for (i in 1:3) print(i)`?
options: `i <- 1; while (i <= 3) { i <- i + 1; print(i) }`
`i <- 1; while (i <= 3) { print(i) }; i <- i + 1`
`i <- 1; while (i <= 3) { print(i); i <- i + 1 }`
`i <- 0; while (i <= 3) { print(i); i <- i + 1 }`

questions.question: What does R print for `g` after `a <- 9; g <- 1; k <- 0; while (k < 2) { g <- 0.5 * (g + a / g); k <- k + 1 }; g`?
Meant to add all elements of `x <- c(3, 8, 2, 6)`, the loop `i <- 1; s <- 0; while (i < length(x)) { s <- s + x[i]; i <- i + 1 }` is run. What is `s` afterwards?
How many passes does `n <- 6; k <- 0; while (n != 1) { if (n %% 2 == 0) n <- n / 2 else n <- 3 * n + 1; k <- k + 1 }` make, that is, what is `k` afterwards?
To define everything before the loop, a student writes `change <- 0; tol <- 1e-6` and then `while (change > tol) { ... }`, where the body updates the guess and `change`. What happens?
options: The loop runs as intended, since the body overwrites `change` in the first pass.
R stops with an error, because `change` has to be positive before the loop starts.
The loop never ends, because `change` starts below `tol` and only decreases.
The body runs zero times, since `0 > tol` is `FALSE` at the first check.

questions.question: To find the first negative element, a student runs `x <- c(4, 7, 2); i <- 1; while (x[i] >= 0) i <- i + 1`. What happens?
options: The loop ends with `i` equal to 3, the position of the last element.
R stops with the error `missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed`.
The loop ends with `i` equal to 4, one position past the end of `x`.
The loop never ends, because no element of `x` is negative.

questions.question: A debt of 1000 grows by 10% interest each year, after which 300 is paid: `d <- 1000; t <- 0; while (d > 0) { d <- d * 1.1 - 300; t <- t + 1 }`. What is `t` afterwards?
What is `g` after `g <- 1; iter <- 0; change <- 100; while (change > 0.01 & iter < 3) { new <- g / 2 + 1; change <- abs(new - g); g <- new; iter <- iter + 1 }`?
